requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change hardens TypeCollector so the analyzer no longer throws when a [MessagePackObject] type has mixed key kinds or duplicate keys. It adds `continue` after the mixed-key diagnostic and guards the int/string member dictionary `Add` calls with `ContainsKey`, in both the property loop and the field loop. It adds analyzer tests for SuppressSourceGeneration types, two execution tests and a README section.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stopped working for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types in 3.1.1. The agent's fix assumes the cause was an exception during member collection (Dictionary.Add on a duplicate key, or `intKey!.Value` on a mismatched key kind) that stopped all diagnostics. No code that checks SuppressSourceGeneration was touched, so whether this is the real root cause cannot be confirmed from the diff.
touches_beyond_requirement: The `continue` and ContainsKey guards change analyzer and generator behaviour for all MessagePackObject types, not only suppressed ones.
README gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents which diagnostics apply. MsgPack012 is listed there but has no test.
Execution tests check generator output and the dynamic-resolver round trip, not the analyzer.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the property-path crash fixes work: each has a targeted test. Low for the field-path changes: no test uses duplicate or mixed keys on fields. Low-to-medium that this fixes the reported regression, because the diff never touches SuppressSourceGeneration handling. The positive diagnostic tests (MsgPack004/015/003) would only show the regression is fixed if they failed before the change, and that cannot be seen here.

claims.text: In the property loop, a member whose key kind differs from the first member's now gets MsgPack005 and is skipped with `continue`. Previously execution fell through to `intKey!.Value` / string handling with a null key.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

breaker.reason: Line 1008 adds `continue;` after reporting `DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys` (MsgPack005), and `intKey!.Value` at line 1019 was previously hit when `isIntKey && intKey == null`. However, in the property loop line 1028 is `else if (stringKey is not null)` (unlike the bare `else` in the field loop at line 1168), so when `!isIntKey && stringKey == null` execution previously skipped the string-key block rather than entering string handling with a null key, falling through directly to line 1045. In addition, `MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure` (lines 125-144) only tests `[Key(0)]` followed by `[Key("Member2")]`, not the string-first direction.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: Line 1008 adds `continue;` after reporting `DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys` (MsgPack005), and `intKey!.Value` at line 1019 was previously hit when `isIntKey && intKey == null`. However, in the property loop line 1028 is `else if (stringKey is not null)` (unlike the bare `else` in the field loop at line 1168), so when `!isIntKey && stringKey == null` execution previously skipped the string-key block rather than entering string handling with a null key, falling through directly to line 1045. In addition, `MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure` (lines 125-144) only tests `[Key(0)]` followed by `[Key("Member2")]`, not the string-first direction.

Claim C15 disputed: Over-citation: `README.md` lines 1622-1623 make substantive claims about formatter suppression, runtime serialization via reflection-based dynamic resolvers, and lack of AOT safety that C15 does not describe (C15 only mentions analyzer rules). Furthermore, whether `MsgPack012` at line 1630 actually applies to `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types is neither shown in the diff nor covered by any test.

Nothing in the diff touches how SuppressSourceGeneration types are handled. If the 3.1.1 regression was that the analyzer skips suppressed types, rather than throwing on key collisions, this change does not fix it. The diff cannot show whether MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported failed before the change.

In the field loop, the string-key branch's Add call (after line 1170) is not shown with a ContainsKey guard, unlike the property loop. If it is still unguarded, duplicate string keys on fields can still crash the analyzer. The field-path changes (1148, 1163-1166) have no test at all.

`continue` skips the rest of the member processing, including the MessagePackFormatter attribute lookup and later member-type checks. Diagnostics such as MsgPack003 on that member are therefore no longer reported while MsgPack005 is present.

Duplicate string keys in the field loop are still unguarded. Unlike property int keys (lines 1023-1026), property string keys (lines 1039-1042), and field int keys (lines 1163-1166), the field loop's `else` branch for string keys (starting at line 1168) was not updated to guard `stringMembers.Add` with `!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)`. A `[MessagePackObject]` type (with or without `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`) that has duplicate `[Key("...")]` string keys on two fields, or on a property and a field, will still throw `ArgumentException` from `stringMembers.Add` and crash the analyzer/generator.
